text: National home prices slip negative for the first time in over two years. High-frequency data shows softening demand, uneven regional movements, and weak builder sentiment. Mortgage-rate stasis limits directional motion, producing a narrow, low-variance band around zero.

meta.note: Exposure vs. collapse boundary thin; compression dominant but ambiguous threshold.

text: U.S. home prices turned negative year-over-year for the first time in over two years, reflecting affordability compression, weak demand, and slight inventory normalization. Regional divergence exposes uneven pressure while mortgage-rate stagnation prolongs drift, flattening the market into a near-zero growth band rather than initiating systemic housing collapse.

meta.note: A soft inversion, not crisis: price flattening absorbs accumulated pandemic distortion within a low-variance compression corridor.
